foods.name: Hard cheeses
foods.why: Hard cheese is too dry and salty for listeria to throw a party in. Cheddar, parmesan and the whole firm crew are a straight yes.

foods.name: Processed cheese slices
foods.why: Pasteurised and sealed, so slices are good to go. Once the pack is open, keep it in the fridge and eat it within a couple of days.

foods.name: Cheese spread
foods.why: Pasteurised and shelf stable until you open it, so spread it on thick. Into the fridge after opening and follow the label.

foods.name: Cream cheese
foods.why: Pasteurised, so it is a yes on your bagel. Keep it cold and finish it within about 2 days of opening, same as any fresh dairy.

foods.name: Cottage cheese
foods.why: Pasteurised and fine, protein and all. Keep it in the fridge with the lid on and finish it within a couple of days of opening.

foods.name: Paneer
foods.why: Paneer is made from pasteurised milk and it almost always turns up cooked and hot. Two ticks in the one curry.

foods.name: Haloumi
foods.why: Cooked until it squeaks and served hot is exactly the safe way with haloumi. Grill it or pan fry it rather than eating it cold from the pack.

foods.name: Melted mozzarella
foods.why: Bubbling on a pizza or baked right through a dish, the heat has done the work for you. Melted mozzarella is a green light.

foods.name: Pasteurised milk
foods.why: Pasteurisation is the whole point: it has already been heat treated for you. Fridge milk or long life off the shelf, both a yes.

foods.name: Yoghurt
foods.why: Every pasteurised kind is a yes, live cultures included. Greek, natural, flavoured or pot set: pick your favourite and dig in.

foods.name: Cream and butter
foods.why: Pasteurised cream and butter are a straight yes: whipped, thickened, soured or spread thick on hot toast. Normal fridge rules apply.

foods.name: Custard
foods.why: Shop-bought custard is pasteurised and ready to pour. Eat it freshly opened, keep it in the fridge and use it within a day.

foods.name: Ice cream from a tub
foods.why: Tub and packaged ice cream is pasteurised and sealed, so it is a yes. The tub is the trick: it is soft serve from a machine that is the problem.

foods.name: Milkshake made at home
foods.why: Pasteurised milk, tub ice cream and your own clean blender: you control the hygiene end to end, so blend away.

foods.name: Brie and camembert
foods.why: Brie careful: soft white-mould cheeses hold moisture, and listeria likes that. Cold from the board they are benched for now.
foods.makeItGreen: Cooked right through and served bubbling hot, baked brie and camembert are back on the menu.
foods.swap: Build the board from hard cheeses instead: cheddar, gouda, parmesan, a bit of quince paste.

foods.name: Feta and ricotta
foods.why: Soft cheeses can carry listeria when they are eaten cold. Baked into something hot, they are completely back on the menu.
foods.makeItGreen: Baked through a hot dish: spanakopita, lasagne, a ricotta pasta bake, served steaming.
foods.swap: Crumble hard cheese over the salad, or go for cottage cheese or cream cheese from the fridge.

foods.name: Blue cheese
foods.why: Blue cheese is a soft, moist cheese, which is exactly the room listeria likes. Cold on a cheese board it is a no for now.
foods.makeItGreen: Melted into a sauce or cooked in a dish and served properly hot, blue cheese is fine.
foods.swap: A sharp aged cheddar or a shave of pecorino gives you the same salty hit.

foods.name: Fresh mozzarella, burrata and bocconcini
foods.why: These fresh cheeses are soft and full of moisture, and that is where listeria settles. Eaten cold and uncooked they are out for now.
foods.makeItGreen: Cooked right through to 75 degrees and eaten hot, on a pizza or baked in a dish, it is a yes.
foods.swap: Melted mozzarella on a hot pizza, or shaved hard cheese over the tomatoes and basil.

foods.name: Soft goat cheese
foods.why: Soft goat cheese is moist and mould ripened, so it sits with brie and feta on the not-right-now list while it is cold.
foods.makeItGreen: Baked or grilled until it is hot right through, like a warm goat cheese tart, and it is back on.
foods.swap: A hard goat gouda, or aged cheddar crumbled over the beetroot salad.

foods.name: Soft serve ice cream
foods.why: It is not the ice cream, it is the machine. Soft serve dispensers are fiddly to clean and listeria can settle inside them.
foods.swap: A scoop from a sealed tub at home, or frozen-banana nice cream in a cone.

foods.name: Thickshakes and McFlurry
foods.why: Same story as soft serve: these all come out of a dispensing machine that is tricky to clean, and listeria can hide in the works.
foods.swap: Blend your own thick shake at home with tub ice cream and cold milk.

foods.name: Scooped gelato
foods.why: Gelato is scooped from tubs, so the risk sits well below soft serve. The unknown is the shared scoop and the bench it rests on.
foods.makeItGreen: Ask for a fresh scoop from a covered tub, or take a sealed tub home from the freezer aisle.
foods.swap: Tub ice cream at home, or a frozen-banana nice cream.

foods.name: Fried ice cream
foods.why: The batter is usually egg based and the fry is quick on purpose, to keep the middle frozen. That means the egg may never cook through.
foods.swap: Tub ice cream under a hot chocolate sauce, or a warm baked pudding with a scoop on the side.

foods.name: Unpasteurised milk and raw-milk cheese
foods.why: With no pasteurisation there is nothing standing between you and listeria, salmonella or E. coli. This one is a firm no for now.
foods.makeItGreen: The pasteurised version of the very same thing is a green light.
foods.swap: Pasteurised milk, and cheese made from pasteurised milk: cheddar, gouda, parmesan.
